address-validation.title: Address Validation
address-validation.responsibility: Check that an address exists and is deliverable, and return it in a standard form.
address-validation.boundaries: It assesses addresses; it doesn't decide which address is a person's or organization's address of record.

operations.name: Address.validate
operations.description: Check and standardize an address.

signs: Notices come back undeliverable.
Each form validates addresses differently, or not at all.
questions: How often are notices returned as undeliverable?

approval.title: Approval
approval.responsibility: Route a decision to a person with the authority to make it, and record the decision, the reasons, and who made it.
approval.boundaries: The business program establishes who has authority for each decision; Approval enforces and records it. An agent may prepare a recommendation, but a consequential decision needs an authorized person.

operations.name: Approval.request
operations.description: Ask for a decision from someone with the authority to make it.

operations.name: Approval.decide
operations.description: Record an approver's decision and reasons.

operations.name: Approval.getStatus
operations.description: Report where a request stands and who it is waiting on.

signs: Approvals happen by email reply.
The same decision goes up two or three levels.
Nobody can show who approved something, or when.
questions: Which decisions need approval, and who may give it?
Where do requests most often wait for a decision?

case-management.title: Case Management
case-management.responsibility: Keep a matter's people, information, tasks, decisions, and history together from receipt to closure, with one accountable owner at a time.
case-management.boundaries: Each program defines its own case types, rules, and completion criteria; Case Management gives them a common model to build on. It links to documents, people, and tasks held by other capabilities rather than owning them.

operations.name: Case.create
operations.description: Open a case from a matter, with its source and case type.

operations.name: Case.get
operations.description: Return the view of a case that the requester may see.

operations.name: Case.assign
operations.description: Give the case an accountable owner, and record the change.

operations.name: Case.link
operations.description: Link related cases while each keeps its own history.

operations.name: Case.recordDecision
operations.description: Record a decision with its reasons, evidence, and decision-maker.

operations.name: Case.close
operations.description: Record the outcome and close the case, keeping its history.

signs: Each program keeps its own case tracker or spreadsheet.
Staff re-key the same matter into more than one system.
Nobody can say who owns a case after it changes hands.
questions: Which systems hold cases, or records that work like cases, today?
Do different teams mean different things by a case?

document-management.title: Document Management
document-management.responsibility: Store, classify, version, and retrieve documents and files, and apply the records rules that govern them.
document-management.boundaries: It knows how a document is classified, secured, retained, and retrieved. The consuming process decides which documents belong to its work and which one is the official version.

operations.name: Document.store
operations.description: Store a document with its classification and the record it belongs to.

operations.name: Document.get
operations.description: Return a document the requester may see, and record the retrieval.

operations.name: Document.classify
operations.description: Set or change a document's classification and access restrictions.

operations.name: Document.applyRetention
operations.description: Apply a records schedule, and hold, transfer, or dispose of the document as it allows.

signs: Case files live on shared drives and personal laptops.
Nobody is sure which copy of a document is the official one.
Retention is applied by hand, or not at all.
questions: Where do documents for this work live today, and who can change them?
Which records schedules apply, and who applies them?

identity.title: Identity
identity.responsibility: Establish who or what is acting, whether staff, a member of the public, a partner, or an agent, and with what level of assurance.
identity.boundaries: Identity says who is acting. What they may do is an authorization decision, made under enterprise policy using that identity.

operations.name: Identity.authenticate
operations.description: Sign a person, system, or agent in.

operations.name: Identity.verify
operations.description: Check evidence that a person is who they claim to be.

operations.name: Identity.getAttributes
operations.description: Return the attributes of an identity that a consumer may use, such as role and organization.

signs: Applications keep their own user accounts and passwords.
External partners share accounts, or can't get one.
Accounts stay active after people change jobs.
questions: How do staff, the public, and partners sign in today, and to how many systems?
Which actions need a higher level of identity assurance?

notification.title: Notification
notification.responsibility: Deliver approved messages to people through their preferred channels, and report whether each one was delivered.
notification.boundaries: The consuming process decides what to say and to whom; Notification delivers it. The process keeps the message in its own record when the message is part of that record.

operations.name: Notification.send
operations.description: Send an approved message to a recipient.

operations.name: Notification.getStatus
operations.description: Report whether a message was delivered, opened, or failed.

signs: Several systems each send their own email.
Nobody can say whether a notice was delivered.
People can't choose how they're contacted.
questions: Which systems send messages to staff, the public, or partners today?
Do any notices have legal or records requirements?

organization-information.title: Organization Information
organization-information.responsibility: Provide an authorized view of an organization, such as a company, vendor, grantee, or agency, from the authoritative records, and match new information to it.
organization-information.boundaries: It reads and matches; it changes an authoritative record only where its owner has agreed. Registration and vendor management processes own their own records.

operations.name: Organization.lookup
operations.description: Find organizations that match identifying details.

operations.name: Organization.get
operations.description: Return the view of an organization that the requester may see.

operations.name: Organization.match
operations.description: Say whether new details belong to an existing organization.

signs: Vendors and grantees are recorded separately in each program.
Nobody can list every case involving the same company.
questions: Which system is authoritative for vendors, grantees, and other organizations?

payment.title: Payment
payment.responsibility: Take and make payments, and report their status, under the enterprise's financial controls.
payment.boundaries: The financial system of record keeps the ledger. Programs decide what is owed or payable; Payment carries it out and reports back.

operations.name: Payment.request
operations.description: Request a payment to or from a person or organization.

operations.name: Payment.getStatus
operations.description: Report whether a payment is pending, made, or failed.

signs: Staff check payment status in a separate financial system.
Several programs integrate with the financial system in different ways.
questions: Does this work take or make payments, and through which systems?

person-information.title: Person Information
person-information.responsibility: Provide an authorized view of a person from the authoritative records, and match new information to a person the enterprise already knows.
person-information.boundaries: It reads and matches; it changes an authoritative record only where its owner has agreed. Each program still decides what it needs to know about a person and why.

operations.name: Person.lookup
operations.description: Find people who match identifying details.

operations.name: Person.get
operations.description: Return the view of a person that the requester may see for a stated purpose.

operations.name: Person.match
operations.description: Say whether new details belong to an existing person, and how confident the match is.

signs: The same person has different identifiers in different systems.
Staff search several systems to find someone's current details.
questions: Which system is authoritative for each kind of person: employees, members of the public, partners?
How do you tell whether two records describe the same person?

reporting.title: Reporting
reporting.responsibility: Provide measures and views of the work from authoritative data, such as workload, age, status, and results, with consistent definitions.
reporting.boundaries: It reports from the systems of record and doesn't become another source of truth. Each measure has an owner and an agreed definition.
reporting.note: Not among the capability map's examples. Added because oversight and statistics need it in almost every program.

operations.name: Report.get
operations.description: Return a measure or view, filtered to what the requester may see.

operations.name: Report.schedule
operations.description: Produce a report on a schedule and deliver it.

signs: Statistics are reconciled by hand in spreadsheets.
Each office counts the same thing differently.
Supervisors can't see workload without asking.
questions: How long does it take to answer a question like “how many cases did we close last year?”
Who defines each measure, and who checks it?

scheduling.title: Scheduling
scheduling.responsibility: Find availability and book, change, and cancel appointments between staff, the public, and partners.
scheduling.boundaries: It manages time and attendance; the consuming process records what an appointment was for and what happened in it.

operations.name: Schedule.findAvailability
operations.description: Find times when the required people and resources are free.

operations.name: Schedule.book
operations.description: Book an appointment and invite the participants.

operations.name: Schedule.change
operations.description: Move or cancel an appointment and tell the participants.

signs: Interviews and appointments are arranged over several emails.
Missed appointments aren't recorded anywhere.
questions: How are interviews and appointments arranged today?

search.title: Search
search.responsibility: Find records, documents, people, and organizations across the enterprise, limited to what the requester may see.
search.boundaries: It finds and points to information; the systems of record stay authoritative. Results respect each record's access rules.

operations.name: Search.query
operations.description: Search within a scope, returning only results the requester may see.

operations.name: Search.findRelated
operations.description: Suggest records that may be related to a given one.

signs: Staff ask colleagues whether a related case exists.
Searching means opening several systems one by one.
questions: Before starting work, how do staff check what the organization already knows?
How far back, and across which systems, can they search?

signature.title: Signature
signature.responsibility: Collect signatures on documents and decisions, and let anyone with access verify them later.
signature.boundaries: It records who signed and protects the signed document from change. Whether a signature is legally sufficient for a given purpose is a policy question.

operations.name: Signature.request
operations.description: Ask one or more people to sign a document.

operations.name: Signature.verify
operations.description: Confirm who signed a document and that it hasn't changed since.

signs: Documents are printed, signed, and scanned.
Signed versions are hard to tell apart from drafts.
questions: Which documents need a signature, and of what kind?

workflow.title: Workflow
workflow.responsibility: Coordinate tasks across people and systems: who does what, by when, and what happens when it's late.
workflow.boundaries: It moves work and tracks it. Who has authority to decide belongs to Approval and enterprise policy, and the rules of each process belong to the program that owns it.

operations.name: Task.create
operations.description: Create a task with an assignee and a due date.

operations.name: Task.assign
operations.description: Assign or reassign a task, keeping its history.

operations.name: Task.complete
operations.description: Record a task's result.

operations.name: Task.escalate
operations.description: Raise an overdue or stalled task to the right person.

signs: Work is tracked in email, personal lists, and spreadsheets.
Overdue work turns up in meetings instead of being flagged.
Each application has its own task list.
questions: How does someone know what they need to do today, and what is overdue?
What happens when a task waits on someone outside the team?
